relations.statement: No local operator moves an isolated fracton: any single-fracton hop requires creating further excitations, so fracton_hop is not a free (energy-preserving) move.
relations.hypotheses: X-cube Hamiltonian, local operators, excitation content of cube-violating stabilizers; imported literature assumption

relations.statement: A fracton dipole can be moved by a local operator only within a plane (planon), not out of its plane.
relations.hypotheses: X-cube model; dipole of two fractons separated along an axis; imported literature assumption

relations.statement: A lineon can be moved only along a lattice axis by string operators.

lemmas.statement: Mobility dimension: isolated fracton 0, lineon 1, planon (fracton dipole) 2, as stated in the target; restates the imported assumption only.

near_misses.claim: An isolated fracton can hop freely along an axis like a lineon.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Fracton hop would require a local operator creating a single cube-excitation; by the X-cube conservation structure fractons appear only in pairs/quadruples under local operators, so isolated mobility is rejected.

near_misses.claim: A fracton dipole is mobile in all three dimensions.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Dipole mobility is planar (planon); out-of-plane motion would leave fracton excitations behind.
